steps.title: Set up the equation
steps.say: We want the x-values that make this equation true. It is a quadratic with a = 1, b = −5, c = 6. I'll start with the quadratic formula.

steps.title: Plug into the formula
steps.say: Substitute a, b, and c into x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a.

steps.title: The method is slow
steps.say: The discriminant simplifies to 1, but there are still several steps to finish. Factoring is faster here, so I'll switch.

ops.text: Too many steps. Switch to factoring!

steps.title: Switch to factoring
steps.say: Forget the formula. Find two numbers with product 6 and sum −5. They are −2 and −3.

steps.title: Write the factored form
steps.say: So the left side factors as (x − 2)(x − 3).

steps.title: Solve each factor
steps.say: A product is zero only if one factor is zero, so x − 2 = 0 or x − 3 = 0. That gives x = 2 or x = 3.

steps.title: Check the answers
steps.say: Substitute each value back into the original equation to confirm both give 0.
